thread:
emma: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change (auto-switch on seq_len), we saw a p99 tail spike in prod ~03:20 UTC. p95 looks fine. flamegraphs point at fallback into the generic matmul kernel for ~7% of steps, which coincides with long-seq requests. @mike can you pull the canary logs?

mike: I was looking earlier. The canary had a microbatch size bump (8->16) rolled in the same deploy. Synthetic loadgen we ran (uniform seq lengths) didn't show the spike. suspect interaction between microbatch sizing + mixed seq distribution + KV cold prefixes.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout redwood-runtime v3.4.1 -> canary completed at 2026-03-17T03:15:00Z :rocket:

emma: exact timeline lines up — kernel-selector change + microbatch bump. KV cache hitrate dropped briefly during the spike window (warmup churn).

sophia: Repro plan: we should do a real-traffic replay that preserves arrival times and KV prefix state. Synthetic uniform seq tests mask the long-tail. Also run a microbatch sweep (4,8,12,16) under the replay.

sophia: example replay command:
```
./replay_tool --source s3://replays/2026-03-16-prod --preserve-kv-warmup --rate-scale 1.0 --microbatch 8 --keep-arrival-pattern
```
Use HDR hist for percentiles.

harry: +1 to replay. Also instrument per-request kernel-choice tag in traces so we can correlate kernel version -> latency bucket. Right now logs show only aggregate counts.

mike: added a quick patch to the selector to emit `kernel_choice` in trace; will push to canary in 30m. Also will run a replay with microbatch 8 vs 16.

liz: for SLOs: we usually tune p95, but customer-facing UX is p99-sensitive. We need to capture both. For benchmarking methodology: replay gives signal for tail under real mix; synthetic is useful for isolating factors but dangerous for rollouts if used alone.

emma: Agreed. Some concrete measurement rules proposed: 1) do arrival-preserving replay for any rollout that touches selector/microbatch/kv; 2) report p50/p95/p99 with HDR hist and explicit sample counts; 3) include KV-hit-rate curve during warmup window; 4) run microbatch sweep and plot tail amplification (p99_ratio = p99(mb)/p99(mb=4)).

harry: Also note down how we compute percentiles: avoid naive aggregations across machines. Use mergeable hdr hist or t-digest with per-shard correction. Otherwise p99 is biased.

mike: ran quick local replay. Preliminary: microbatch=16 increases average throughput but p99 worsens 18% vs mb=8 when mixed seqs present. KV-warmup spike causes the selector to reroute to generic kernel under load; that increases compute time per token.

emma: Action items: (1) mike — run full-preserve replay sweep and upload HDR hist output to /artifacts/runtime/replays/1768712345/, (2) sophia — add KB doc on replay flags and kv-warmup preservation, (3) harry — add kernel_choice tag to tracing schema, (4) liz — update rollout checklist to require replay if selector/microbatch/kv touched.

liz: can we also add a canary shadow for 10% prod traffic for next deploy as a safety net?

emma: yes. I'll schedule it. Thanks all :eyes: 

mike: filing a short postmortem note after the replay runs, will include graphs. :+1:
